title: Archie Weatherspoon V Commits as Cal Poly Men's Basketball's Top Recruit Ever - Mustang News
content:
Cal Poly Men’s Basketball has officially landed its highest-rated recruit in program history in combo guard Archie Weatherspoon V. Weatherspoon V, who attends Rangeview High School in Aurora, Colo., announced on Sunday that he plans to join the Mustangs next season. Weatherspoon V is a three-star recruit according to 247Sports and is ranked the 247th player in the country and the third-highest in the state of Colorado. The 6-foot-3 guard held offers from programs such as Cal, Creighton, UNLV and High Point but ultimately opted to join Head Coach Mike DeGeorge and the Mustangs. With a 247Sports composite rating of .8950, Weatherspoon V surpasses Brantly Stevenson (2020) as the outlet’s highest-ranked Cal Poly recruit in history. DeGeorge’s previous coaching stint at Colorado Mesa gave him familiarity with Weatherspoon V’s home state, a potential advantage while recruiting against higher-profile programs. Weatherspoon V profiles as a potential lead guard while remaining a high-level scoring threat, using his 6-foot-8 wingspan to slice through defenses and get to the basket. Weatherspoon V has been highly efficient at the high school level and possesses a clean, repeatable shooting form. Weatherspoon V averaged 19.2 points, 4.0 rebounds, 3.7 assists and 1.6 steals per game across 26 games in his junior season. He is the first verbal commitment that the Mustangs have gotten in this recruiting cycle. Oliver Marburg is the sports copy editor for Mustang News. title: Fallen trooper recognized before North Schuylkill v. Mount Carmel football game - shensentinel.com
content: KAYLEE LINDENMUTH / SHENANDOAH SENTINEL - The Pahira family makes their way to midfield. FOUNTAIN SPRINGS – A fallen hero was prominently honored at his alma mater Friday night. Trooper Michael Pahira, a North Schuylkill graduate and former Spartan football player, died in a fatal crash earlier this year. His jersey number, 74, was prominently displayed atop the visitor’s press box and alight throughout the night. Prior to the game, the Pahira family was presented with his #74 jersey and a ball signed by the 2026 North Schuylkill football team. Pahira’s parents presented the game ball to the referees in pregame ceremonies and conducted the coin toss. Three state troopers from Pahira’s Frackville barracks joined them. As the coin toss wrapped up, a State Police helicopter, Trooper 1, became visible atop Broad Mountain. It lined up for the field and conducted a flyover to astounding applause throughout the stadium. title: Michael Carrick details why one Red is unavailable for Fulham v Man Utd but stays tight-lipped on one absentee - Yahoo Sports
content: Michael Carrick is without two players who featured in Manchester United's midweek defeat to Brighton and Hove Albion. Indeed, Ayden Heaven and Benjamin Sesko have both been omitted from the matchday squad at Craven Cottage. Speaking to the media ahead of kick-off, Carrick confirmed that Sesko had felt a slight injury following the Carabao Cup tie, so he decided it was best to leave him out this afternoon. "A little bit of an assessment at the moment. He pulled up after the game the other day with a little bit of pain, so we'll have to see how he is," said the manager. The Slovenian is United's only out-and-out centre-forward in the side this season, but he has still yet to start a Premier League fixture, with his only two starts of the term coming in the League Cup and Champions League. Elsewhere, Ayden Heaven is nowhere to be seen on the teamsheet, despite being fit and available. He travelled with his teammates to London, but will travel back at full-time without playing any minutes in the clash with the Cottagers. It's thought that his absence is due to Carlos Baleba being deemed match-fit on the day of the game, hence his inclusion on the bench instead. Heaven did oversee a particularly dismal display in the loss to the Seagulls, so he was presumably in line to lose his starting spot anyway. After this weekend, fans will have to wait three weeks to see United back in action due to the lengthy international break. Did make a remarkable goalline clearance to prevent an own goal. 5 Marc Guehi: Will have an assist alongside his name but an otherwise uncomfortable afternoon for the England international. 5 Josko Gvardiol: Failed to close down Enzo le Fee for Sunderland's second goal but provided the cross for Erling Haaland's goal. 6 Elliot Anderson: The former Newcastle man was jeered throughout by the travelling Sunderland fans, but made more passes than any other player on the pitch. 6 Enzo Fernandez: Curled in a delightful free-kick for his first City goal and the crafty Argentine saw plenty of the ball in the pockets outside the box. Becoming a fans' favourite with the "Enzo, Enzo" chant. 7 Iliman Ndiaye: Started in place of the suspended Phil Foden and was lively throughout. Unlucky not to get an assist after laying a ball on to Erling Haaland with the goal gaping. 6 Antoine Semenyo: Back in form. Twice thumped home for his first goals of the season and kept the ball alive to poke through a pass for Rayan Cherki's goal. 9 Rayan Cherki: Near his best in this game with some delightful touches. Quick feet and trickery helped create City's opener, and stayed cool to stroke home City's second goal in the first half. 8 Erling Haaland: Sunderland had been the only Premier League team the Norwegian had not scored against. Looked like staying that way when he missed an easy opportunity in the first half but he ended that run with a finish late on. 6 Jeremy Doku (on 74, Ndiaye): Returned from a calf injury for his first league minutes this season. 6 Nico O'Reilly (on 85, Cherki): Should have scored seconds after coming on. 6 Subs not used: Rulli, Kovacic, Ait-Nouri, Bouaddi, Allan, Khusanov, Lewis Robin Roefs: Will be disappointed for the first goal. Tried to anticipate Fernandez sending in a cross but instead found himself being beaten at his near post. 4 Nordi Mukiele: A tough game up against Semenyo, who scored twice. 5 Kevin Danso: Poor clearance contributed to City winning the ball back high up the pitch for Cherki's goal. 5 Dan Ballard: Part of a backline that conceded three goals in the opening 45 minutes. 5 Dayann Methalie: Booked inside 10 minutes of his Premier League debut and given a difficult game by Ndiaye. 5 Granit Xhaka: The skipper helped his side get back on level terms twice in the game, but ultimately went home with nothing. 6 Noah Sadiki: Eyes opened up when he found space to shoot after darting forward, but blazed his effort high and wide. 6 Thomas Meunier: The former Belgium international could have had a shot for the second goal but instead laid it on a plate for Brobbey to finish. 7 Enzo le Fee: The French passmaster fizzed a lovely ball into the feet of Brobbey for Sunderland's equaliser and his cleverly disguised pass led to his side's second. 8 Nilson Angulo: Could have made a name for himself but scuffed a golden chance wide in the opening five minutes. Provided the assist for Brobbey's third goal. 6 Brian Brobbey: The hat-trick hero. title: CR-V Laps The RAV4, And Honda Isn't Coasting - thetruthaboutcars.com
content: Toyota's all-new, all-hybrid RAV4 was supposed to spend 2026 doing what the RAV4 always does: sit near the top of the sales charts as the best-selling thing in America that isn't an F-Series. Fresh styling, more power, better efficiency. Instead, production problems knocked sales down early in the year, and the Honda CR-V walked right through the open door. Honda's lead is now large enough that Toyota probably can't reel it back before the calendar runs out. Rather than sit on that advantage, Honda appears to be pressing it. According to Japanese outlet Nikkei, production of a new-generation CR-V hybrid starts in Canada in February, with the Indiana and Ohio plants following in March. That points to cars reaching dealers before summer, sooner than the previously expected late-2026 window. That's a quick turnaround for a model that's only been on sale since the 2023 model year. The changes run deep. Honda's compact and midsize hybrid family — Civic, CR-V, and Accord — has been in line for a reworked architecture and drivetrain, previewed by a running prototype late last year. The new chassis is lighter and reportedly up to 10 percent cheaper to build. The powertrain keeps a naturally aspirated 2.0-liter four but adds direct injection and new electric motors for efficiency. Honda is also porting over the Prelude's simulated shifting, some power-control tricks meant to aid handling, and reportedly a sportier exhaust note. The RAV4 may well recover once Toyota gets production back to full pace. But a cheaper, more efficient CR-V isn't the only thing waiting for it. Nissan is launching its first hybrid Rogue in years, on an entirely new platform that will later spawn a combustion version. Hyundai has revealed a new Tucson for next year, bigger and with more distinctive styling. Today's RAV4 amounts to a substantial update of the outgoing car rather than a clean-sheet design. Notably, both Honda and Nissan are prioritizing the hybrid variants. With gas prices spiking, that timing looks less like a coincidence and more like where the segment is heading. title: The Only Manual, V8, Rear-Wheel Drive Sedan Left In The USA Now Produces 685 HP - CarBuzz
content: Subscribe to the CarBuzz newsletter to never miss an update The golden age of the V8 performance sedan felt like it would last forever — a supercharged engine up front, three pedals on the floor, five seats, and power routed strictly to the rear wheels. That formula produced some of the most celebrated driver's cars ever made, and for a while, the options were plentiful. Today, the market has moved on almost entirely. Electrification, all-wheel drive, and turbocharged six-cylinders have replaced the old recipe — almost. In 2026, exactly one sedan on sale in the United States still checks every box: the Cadillac CT5-V Blackwing. By now, you know the CT5-V Blackwing's headline figures, with the supercharged 6.2-liter V8 pumping out a thunderous 668 horsepower and 659 lb-ft of torque. While the BMW M5 and performance sedans of its ilk have paired that much power with AWD for the better part of a decade, Cadillac's refusal to drive the front axle is admirable. But making the manual standard? That's worthy of a parade through the streets. The manual is a six-speed unit sourced from transmission specialists Tremec, featuring No-Lift Shift functionality and Active Rev-Matching for the most performance possible from a car with three pedals. With one of the most beautifully balanced chassis, a long wheelbase, keen steering, and the ability to row gears yourself, the CT5-V Blackwing makes a strong case for being crowned one of the best performance sedans ever built. The only problem is that this has officially been declared the final send-off for the ICE-powered Cadillac V-Series, and while the manual was retained for the facelift (thanks to a nearly 50 percent take rate for the six-speed in 2023), when the CT5-V Blackwing thunders off into the night, it'll take that six-speed with it. For 2026, Cadillac introduced the CT5-V Blackwing F1 Collector Series, celebrating the brand's first Grand Prix in the USA. It's not a phone-in special edition, either. In addition to distinctive design features, Cadillac fitted a new supercharger that lifts output to 685 hp and 673 lb-ft of torque. Only 26 will be built, and it's virtually guaranteed to appreciate in value. The standard car is already the last of its kind — this is by far the most extreme version of it. People like to hype current models as future classics to artificially inflate their values, but the CT5-V Blackwing might actually have a genuine case. The F1 Collector Series says it right in the name — it's a special variant with more power than the already-impressive standard car, courtesy of a new supercharger, and such a limited production run is sure to drive up values. Setting the rare variant aside, the standard Blackwing holds its value better than most cars. In fact, the debut model year's base MSRP in 2022 was $83,995, and used examples have retained a remarkable share of that figure — only a roughly 10% drop in four years, whereas many other cars lose half their value in a similar timeframe through normal depreciation. Buyers are spending even more on special variants, like the First Edition Series from 2022 (250 units produced) or the 2023 model year's 120-year Anniversary Edition, of which 120 units were produced. We're confident the latest F1 Collector Series will command serious attention at future auctions. While current CT5 production ends in late 2026, General Motors has officially greenlit a second-generation CT5 platform, and reports indicate a next-generation CT5-V Blackwing successor will follow, but nothing has been confirmed. Built on an updated Alpha architecture, the incoming internal combustion luxury sedan is expected to arrive for the 2027 or 2028 model year. While Cadillac has re-evaluated its all-electric timeline, precise powertrain details remain under wraps. Enthusiasts are watching closely to see if GM retains a supercharged V8 and six-speed manual option, or pivots toward a high-output forced-induction or hybrid setup to keep America's ultimate performance sedan alive. Over the last five years, the American automotive industry has undergone a quiet execution of the V8 performance sedan. A segment that once epitomized effortless highway cruising and tire-shredding muscle has been systematically dismantled by tightening emissions mandates, downsizing, and forced induction. Major high-volume staples like the Dodge Charger R/T, Scat Pack, and Hellcat variants—alongside its understated luxury sibling, the Chrysler 300C—were officially retired, taking the legendary Hemi V8 platform down with them. Luxury benchmarks were not spared either; Cadillac dropped the twin-turbo Blackwing V8 in the short-lived CT6-V, leaving only the hand-built, supercharged 6.2-liter CT5-V Blackwing to carry the mantle for domestic four-doors. Beyond Detroit, foreign alternatives like the naturally aspirated Lexus IS 500 F Sport and Mercedes-AMG’s V8 C63 have either bowed out or downsized to complex hybrid setups. Today, the once-flourishing V8 sedan market is reduced to a handful of expensive, low-volume holdouts, shifting real V8 enthusiast demand straight to the pre-owned market. It's fitting for Cadillac to be the last bastion of the rear-wheel-drive V8 sedan, since the automaker has offered so many compelling options throughout its history. Some of its more recent sports sedans — the current CT5-V and CT4-V — use turbocharged six- and four-cylinder engines, respectively. For genuine V8 models, you have to look further back. An often overlooked and increasingly rare example is the STS-V. Sold from the 2006 through 2009 model years, it was powered by a 4.4-liter supercharged V8 producing 469 horsepower and 439 lb-ft of torque. It's not worth much today, having been overshadowed by the less-powerful but more celebrated CTS-V sedan from the same era. While the STS-V lasted only a single generation, the CTS-V went on to achieve genuine icon status, eventually spanning sedan, coupe, and wagon variants. A more modern — and similarly overlooked — model that some readers may not even know about is Cadillac's CT6-V. The CT6 launched for the 2016 model year, and its V-Series variant arrived for just two model years, 2019 and 2020. Under the hood sat a 4.2-liter twin-turbo V8 making 550 hp and 640 lb-ft of torque, sent to the rear wheels through a 10-speed automatic. The 0–60 mph sprint took under four seconds. title: Sutton's predictions: Man City v Sunderland - Yahoo Sports
content: Sunderland are a really good team and, on their day, they are more than a match for anyone. The Black Cats are strong and robust, and when they get after teams and press you then they are phenomenal. All of that makes me think this is a really hard game for Manchester City. Their derby victory was a brilliant win, and Enzo Maresca's biggest result as their manager so far with the way they did it. Iliman Ndiaye showed what a good signing he is when he came on for Rayan Cherki in the second half at Old Trafford, in terms of offering a different profile. Cherki's more of an inside forward, as a number 10 or playing narrow, and he's a guy you think you couldn't get the ball off in a telephone box. Ndiaye, though, will do more work going back and is also more of a ball carrier, so he was exactly what City needed when they went a man down. Manchester United can feel hard done by because City's winner should have been disallowed, but the visitors were the better team with 10 men. This will be a very different task for Maresca's men, with the emphasis on them breaking down the Black Cats, but I don't feel it will just be one-way traffic. I still think City will find a way, though, and they need to for the sake of the title race. They already seem to be the only team capable of keeping pace with Arsenal.

title: La Liga today: How to watch Atlético Madrid v Real Madrid, TV channels & live stream Sunday 20 September - The Guardian
content: How will Atlético Madrid and Real Madrid fare today? Here is what to know, including kick-off time, TV channels and live stream options The first Madrid derby of the season could have a big bearing on the 2026/27 campaign as a whole for Atlético Madrid and Real Madrid with both teams aiming to establish the momentum needed to keep pace with Barcelona at the top of La Liga. Atléti have won two of their last three home La Liga derbies, but are emerging from a transitional summer with several new signings still bedding into Diego Simeone’s side. Even after recent wins over Real Sociedad and Osasuna, their form is unpredictable. Real Madrid have won six of their first seven fixtures in all competitions to start the season, but are still searching for the right tactical balance after the return of José Mourinho as manager. Here is your complete guide on how to watch today’s La Liga fixture, including kick-off times, broadcast networks and online streaming options. There aren’t many teams on Real Madrid’s level as an attacking force. Kylian Mbappé and Vinícius Júnior have combined for 14 goal contributions in La Liga while midfielder Arda Guler has also started the campaign in strong form. Los Blancos have netted 17 goals in six league outings. As a coherent unit, though, Mourinho’s Real Madrid are suffering many of the same issues that brought down Xabi Alonso and Álvaro Arbeloa before him. The 15-time European champions still lack a natural No 6 at the base of the midfield and have kept just one clean sheet in six league games. Atléti are similarly searching for the right balance. Jonathan David, Lee Kang-in, Alejandro Grimaldo and Cristian Romero are still bedding in, but recent wins suggest Simeone has pointed his team in the right direction again. Sunday’s encounter could be an open affair. Player to watch: Kylian Mbappé, Real Madrid – The French forward remains one of the most exhilarating players to watch in world soccer and has started the season in scintillating form. Mbappé could be the difference-maker who gives Real Madrid the derby bragging rights.

title: Atlético Madrid v Real Madrid Prediction: La Liga Preview - Opta Analyst
content:
We look ahead to Sunday’s La Liga game at the Metropolitano with our Atlético Madrid vs Real Madrid prediction and preview. Who will claim bragging rights in the season’s first derby? Just two points separate Atlético Madrid and Real Madrid after six matches in La Liga this season, and both teams will be determined to get one over their rivals before the international break. José Mourinho has enjoyed a largely successful return to Madrid so far, losing just one of his league matches – a shock 1-0 defeat to Real Betis – and winning the other five. Their last-gasp 3-2 win over Elche last time out sent them second, three points behind Barcelona at the top of the table, and another victory over Atlético would ensure they go into the break in a strong position. Atlético are only two points behind their city rivals, so a win would see them leapfrog Madrid, and they are high on confidence after back-to-back wins over Real Sociedad and Osasuna without conceding. But beating Madrid won’t come easy to Diego Simeone; he has lost all three of his La Liga meetings with Mourinho. The only manager against whom he has managed more matches in the competition with a 100% loss rate (five matches, five defeats) is Xavi Hernández. And Madrid have looked particularly strong this season – only Barcelona (28) have scored more than them, while they have the joint-best defensive record (one of nine teams to only concede six times). Madrid have won more points (four) than any other La Liga team from goals scored in the 85th minute or onwards this season. Carlos Espí is responsible for two of those, including the stoppage-time winner against Elche; both of his goals have come in the 90th minute or later. And they of course have Kylian Mbappé leading the line – he already tops Madrid’s scoring charts with seven goals this term. The Frenchman will reach 500 goal involvements at club level (currently 499 – 377 goals, 122 assists) if he scores or assists in this match, and he never needs much of an invitation to fire on goal. After registering just two goals or assists in his first nine La Liga games against Atlético (two assists), Vinícius Júnior has since been directly involved in four goals in his last four league encounters against them (two goals, two assists). Madrid have lost three of their last five away La Liga games against Atlético (W1 D1), though, after suffering just one defeat in their previous 20 visits to the Rojiblancos in the competition (W12 D7). And they have picked up points in eight of their last nine away derbies (W4 D4 L1), but Atlético are on their longest-ever home winning streak in derbies against teams from Madrid (W6). Simeone’s side responded well to consecutive losses to Athletic Club and Liverpool, scoring seven goals with no reply in the two matches since. A worry for Simeone will be that they are the only team to have conceded 100% of their goals (6/6) in the second half of their La Liga matches this season. But given the strength of their attack, this has the opportunity to be a very open encounter if Atlético choose to take the risk. Jonathan David has scored two goals in his first two La Liga games for Atlético, and a Madrid derby goal would cap a brilliant start for him. He could become the first player to score in his first three appearances in the competition for the Rojiblancos in the 21st century. Atlético lost their last La Liga match against Madrid 3-2 in March, ending a six-game unbeaten streak (W2 D4) against them. Atleti have only suffered two or more consecutive defeats against Los Blancos in the competition under Simeone on two occasions: three defeats in 2013 and two defeats in 2020. Madrid have won their last two games against Atlético in all competitions; they’ve not recorded three or more consecutive victories against them since 2013, when they had 10 consecutive wins (two under Manuel Pellegrini and eight under Mourinho). Given Madrid’s recent record against Atlético, they are expected to triumph on Sunday, coming out on top in 46.6% of the supercomputer’s simulations. The Rojiblancos have a 28.3% chance of claiming three points against their city rivals, with a further 25.1% chance of splitting the points in a draw. title: 5 Immediate Takeaways From LSU v. Ole Miss - Sports Illustrated
content: The LSU Tigers were finally kicking off conference play and the first road game of the season, and the program traveled to Oxford, Mississippi, to take on the Ole Miss Rebels in the most anticipated game of the year. The Tigers started sluggish, unable to get anything going on offense, and were being diced up by Trinidad Chambliss and the Rebels' offense, and a few critical injuries certainly slowed them down as well. The offense showed some life, but it was too little too late, and they dropped their first game of the season in a 32-24 thriller. So what five things stood out from the contest? Leavitt was given time in the pocket as the offensive line was finding plenty of success in pass protection, but the Tigers' signal-caller would opt to use his legs early in the development of the plays, rather than taking an extra second or two. It was a continued trend that made it seem like the Tigers couldn't find any rhythm, with him tucking the ball and running often. There were very few downfield throws in the first half because of it, which kept the Rebels from worrying about the field being stretched. It's well known that Kiffin's offense is only as good as its running game, which is why establishing it early is such an emphasis for the offense. However, the Tigers struggled in that aspect, especially in the first half, and despite averaging 3.5 yards per carry, it failed to be consistent in any way. That kept the passing game from being a weapon, as there were no bites on RPO or play-actions, causing more stress on offense. For two weeks in a row now, the Tigers' offense has struggled to find any resemblance to a strong start, the way they did in their blowout week one win. While the struggles last week were because Leavitt threw three interceptions, it put more pressure on the defense. Leavitt didn't throw any interceptions for this one, but the slow start from the offense once again placed pressure on the defense, and this time they slipped facing stronger competition. For as much as the Tigers struggled in the first half, they found a groove in the second half, including a 17-0 run. That marks two weeks since the offense overcame its struggles to become the dominant group everyone expected it to be. Leavitt doubled his passing yards in the second half, finding a groove, stepping up more into the pocket, and becoming more like the signal-caller he was in the first half. While it took a while to get there, it was still nice to see. As the Tigers continue to play more conference opponents, including a trip against the Texas A&M Aggies next week, the second-half adjustments are great to see, but needing fewer of them will be critical. This was the first true road test for the Tigers this season, having spent the first two weeks at home, and they played in perhaps one of the most hostile environments in college football this season considering Kiffin's return. However, the road noise didn't seem to affect them much, and they handled the environment and noise with ease, which will play a critical role as the season continues. title: CR-V Is Destroying RAV4 In America, And Honda Is About To Turn Up The Heat - CarBuzz
content: Subscribe to the CarBuzz newsletter to never miss an update Toyota's new, all-hybrid RAV4 line should've been dominating the sales charts this year. It packed fresh styling, more power, and more efficiency in what was already America's favorite vehicle that wasn't an F-Series. Instead, production woes sent sales plummeting early in the year. That's left an opening for its fiercest rival, the Honda CR-V to overtake it. In fact, the Honda is so far ahead, it's unlikely that Toyota can catch up this year. It seems Honda is wanting to hold onto that lead, since it may be launching a new generation of CR-V even earlier than expected. We've known for some time now that Honda has been working up a revised platform and powertrain for its small to midsize hybrids, which include the Civic, CR-V, and Accord. Honda shared details and even demonstrated a test car late last year. At that time, we were expecting to see either a new hybrid Civic or CR-V appear toward the end of 2026. It now seems certain that the CR-V is probably what we'll see, since Japanese news outlet Nikkei reports that production of the new CR-V hybrid will start in Canada in February, followed by its plants in Indiana and Ohio in March. That probably means vehicles arriving at dealers before summer. This new CR-V hybrid will likely be substantially different from the current model, which is a bit of a surprise considering the current one has only been around since the 2023 model year. The big differences will come from the new chassis, which will be lighter and up to 10% cheaper to produce, as well as the updated powertrain. While it will still use a naturally-aspirated 2.0-liter four-cylinder, it will have some improvements to efficiency from direct fuel injection and new electric motors. Honda is also adding the simulated shifting from the Prelude, some interesting power control tricks to aid handling, and, apparently, a surprisingly sporty exhaust note. Ultimately, the Toyota RAV4 may return to glory, especially once the company finally gets production back up to full pace. However, if the new CR-V hybrid delivers on efficiency and cost improvements on top of its great driving dynamics, Toyota should be worried about losing sales. Even worse, though, is that a new Honda won't be the only thing for the RAV4 to face down. Nissan is about to launch its first hybrid Rogue in years. It's on a completely new platform that will eventually be joined by a combustion-only version in the near future, and our experience with a prototype shows that it has serious potential in the segment. Hyundai has also revealed a completely new Tucson for next year with stand-out styling and it's notably bigger. Depending on how these new models perform, the RAV4, which is a heavily refreshed version of its predecessor, could suddenly be at a disadvantage, right as production starts picking up. Aside from Toyota having some real reasons to worry about the RAV4's position in the compact SUV segment, Honda moving up CR-V production, and especially the hybrid, says something else. It shows how important hybrids are becoming in the market. Even Nissan has prioritized getting the hybrid version of its new Rogue to market before the combustion one. It's also quite possible that demand for hybrids could grow even more now that gas prices are spiking. In fact, Toyota probably isn't the only company that should be concerned about its position in the car market, but so should American automakers that are lacking small hybrid SUVs. title: Climate at the Supreme Court: Suncor v. Boulder | (ACOEL) | American College of Environmental Lawyers - JD Supra
content:
During the spring 2026 semester, I taught Climate Change Law and Policy at the Indiana University McKinney School of Law. The last time I taught the class was in 2021 before I joined the Biden Administration. Boy, how times have changed! Because of actions by the current Administration attempting to dismantle EPA’s regulatory authority over greenhouse gases under the Clean Air Act, including most notably the rescission of the Endangerment Finding, a course that in 2021 required six hours on EPA climate programs required less than half that amount in 2026. I expect I will have more work to do in future years, depending on how the legal challenges to these actions are decided. To prepare for the course, I found myself having to learn new material (imagine!). In particular, I focused on the citizen climate suits, especially Juliana v. United States [see Juliana v. United States, 947 F.3d 1159, 1171 (9th Cir. 2020)], and the numerous efforts by state and local governments to seek damages from the fossil fuel industry through litigation or state legislation. My students and I were inspired by the energy and creativity of the States of Hawaii, Connecticut, Vermont, and New York, the cities of New York and Honolulu, and others, struggling to plan and pay for infrastructure and other solutions to protect their residents, institutions, and businesses from flooding, wildfires, sea level rise, extreme heat, and extreme weather—the increasing impacts of our changing climate. But we were also worn down by their continuous court losses. Industry defendants have successfully argued that the Compact Clause, federal pre-emption, the Dormant Commerce Clause, political questions, and the Supremacy Clause preclude states and local governments from bringing tort claims such as nuisance, trespass, or misrepresentation, or constitutional claims under the public trust doctrine. While increasingly acknowledging the undeniability of harm from climate change caused by emissions of greenhouse gases, courts have mostly thrown up their hands at finding a path to give plaintiffs their day in court. In 2018, the city of Boulder and Boulder County sued various oil and gas companies under state tort law alleging that the companies deceived consumers and the public about the climate harms of their products, seeking damages under state common law. After a five-year battle over whether the case should be removed to federal court, the 10th Circuit decided it should not, Board of County Commissioners of Boulder County v. Suncor Energy (U.S.A.) Inc., 25 F.4th 1238 (10th Cir. 2022), and the Supreme Court denied certiorari. 143 S. Ct. 1795 (2023). The state court denied defendants’ motion to dismiss on federal preemption grounds and the Colorado Supreme Court affirmed. 2025 CO 21. This time, the US Supreme Court decided to hear the case, which will be argued on October 5, 2026. In addition to jurisdictional questions, the substantive question presented is whether federal law precludes a local government from seeking damages under state tort law for misleading the public about the damaging effects of greenhouse gas emissions on the global climate. Dozens of briefs have been filed by amici curiae on both sides, all available at the Supreme Court Docket. Despite the increasingly serious real-world impacts on communities across America, dealing meaningfully with climate change has proven to be impossible for the legislative branch and very challenging for the administrative branch given election cycles, litigation, and the overall political toxicity of the issue. With Boulder v Suncor, the US Supreme Court has the opportunity to decide whether those who are suffering injury and monetary loss have the ability to go to court to prove their case and seek damages. ©

title: Cadillac's $168,000 Escalade-V Packs More Horsepower Than An AMG GLS 63 And Undercuts A Rolls-Royce Cullinan - CarBuzz
content: Subscribe to the CarBuzz newsletter to never miss an update Only a few American luxury automakers remain in business, notably Lucid, Lincoln, and Cadillac. The Lucid Gravity SUV is quick and powerful, which one might expect from an EV. Lincoln focuses on being premium, rather than building high-performance models. Only Cadillac brings a body-on-frame SUV with a supercharged V8 to a competition dominated by German and British performance cars. Mercedes-Benz has the AMG GLS 63, Aston Martin offers the 717-horsepower DBX S, and Rolls-Royce even rules the party with its stately Cullinan. All that said, the Escalade-V is the last unapologetically American entry into a segment controlled by European brands. All specs come directly from the manufacturers. Pricing is correct at the time of writing, and excludes destination, options, taxes, incentives, and other potential dealer fees. Automakers reserve the right to change prices at any time without notice. Excluding Cadillac's actual Rolls-Royce rival, the Celestiq, which starts in the low-$400k range, the Escalade-V is the most expensive model Cadillac currently offers. The base 2027 Escalade-V starts at $169,300 before destination and options, while the long-wheelbase ESV begins at $172,300 for its added interior room. That price is a hard pill to swallow when you consider its competition. The 2026 Mercedes-AMG GLS 63 currently starts at $151,050 before options. A customer could add the Executive Rear Seat package, the Manufaktur custom interior package, and a Burmester 29-speaker 3D audio system, and you'd barely reach the Escalade-V's base price. However, both rivals' prices pale in comparison to the Rolls-Royce Cullinan. It's on an entirely different level of luxury and customization. The Rolls isn't a direct rival to the Escalade-V or the AMG GLS 63. Cadillac isn't afraid of the luxury industry's big names, though, as proven by the Celestiq. That said, the Cullinan starts at around $429,600 before options, which helps put the Escalade-V's price into perspective in this segment. Despite being Cadillac's most expensive SUV, it doesn't hold its value all that well. According to CarEdge, the Escalade in general loses about 58% of its value after its first five years on the road. Of course, the V-Series model may hold value slightly better because it's a more desirable performance variant, but real-world listings for used models show significant depreciation. Using CarBuzz's price trend data, we can see the 2023 Escalade-V (the year this variant debuted) is currently worth about $107,000 on average. That figure accounts for 70 listings posted around the country for a fair average, with the highest asking price reaching $151,440. Nicer examples often go to auction, where owners expect to sell for higher reserves. Online auction data shows the Escalade-V averages $124,067. This includes all model years from 2023 to today, so newer, lower-mileage examples are raising its overall average. On that note, CarEdge also has data on the Mercedes-Benz GLS, which it found depreciates by 48% after five years. The AMG GLS 63 variant may hold value better, simply because it's a more desirable high-performance model. Finally, iSeeCars is another trustworthy source, which finds the Rolls-Royce Cullinan will lose about 38.9% of its value in half a decade. All three models are more powerful than any SUV driver needs, but they produce that power and handle differently. Cadillac uses an existing truck platform to build its body-on-frame model, then equips it with the same engine used in the CT5-V Blackwing. It's a 6.2-liter V8 with a supercharger that boosts its output to 682 horsepower and 653 lb-ft of torque. A 10-speed automatic transmission sends power to all four wheels, which provide enough grip to launch the model to 60 mph from a standstill in a claimed 4.4 seconds. It's quick, but not as quick as you think. Cadillac quotes a sprint from zero to 60 mph taking 4.4 seconds. A few unofficial stopwatch sprints got me there in just under 5 seconds, so I don't doubt the official time. Thing is, the Caddy's force-fed V8 has a lot of mass to get moving... - Christopher Smith, Senior Editor, CarBuzz (2025 Cadillac Escalade-V Drive Review) Some characteristics we highlight in our drive review include its brutally loud exhaust, horrible fuel economy of 13 combined mpg, and aggressive road presence from sharper styling than the regular Escalade. It also handles fairly well for a 6,361-pound SUV; when in V-mode, steering is tighter, the six-piston Brembo brakes are more sensitive, and its suspension prevents too much body roll around corners. The AMG GLS 63 is no slouch. It's equipped with a 4.0-liter twin-turbo V8 that makes 603 horsepower and 627 lb-ft of torque. A nine-speed dual-clutch automatic transmission sends power to all four wheels, which is smooth enough for a claimed 4.1-second 0-60 mph sprint. Then we have the Cullinan. This high-luxury SUV isn't built for speed, but it's not slow, either. Under the hood is a 6.75-liter twin-turbocharged V12 that makes 563 horsepower and 627 lb-ft of torque, and the Black Badge variant pushes 592 hp and 664 lb-ft of torque. The standard model can sprint to 60 mph in about 5.0 seconds before reaching a limited top speed of 155 mph. General Motors' 6.2-liter V8 has major issues that have been plaguing trucks and SUVs, including the Escalade-V, for a few years. There have been lawsuits and recalls, but even the federal government is tired of hearing about it. GM's recalls haven't totally fixed the issues, and bad engines keep coming out of the factory. Nevertheless, buyers keep choosing Chevrolet, GMC, and Cadillac models like this one. Even if your engine is free of factory machining debris, you'll still be on the hook for luxury SUV-worthy maintenance costs. CarEdge data shows owners are paying an average of $4,803 in maintenance and repair costs over their first five years on the road. That's $1,657 less than the average luxury SUV and beats both the Mercedes-Benz GLS and Rolls-Royce Cullinan by far. The same source notes a 17.65% chance an Escalade could need a major repair, or a repair costing $500 or more, within its first five years on the road. That's 2.9% better than similar vehicles in its segment. CarEdge also says owners spend $5,940 to maintain and repair their GLSs in their first five years of service. AMG variants could cost slightly more, depending on how aggressively owners drive and treat their models. Harder driving could cause parts to break sooner, leading to higher yearly costs. The Cullinan is a little harder to find averages for, since relatively few are on the road. That said, some dealerships publish their anticipated service costs; one dealer explains how an annual service, including an oil change, tire rotation, and inspecting countless other parts, could cost $4,000. Our road tester explains how the engine might be what everybody wants to hear about, but the Escalade-V's interior may be its best feature. JD Power just named Cadillac the most innovative brand selling cars in the United States, as it stands out in five main categories: comfort and convenience, connected vehicle, driver assist, electric vehicle, and smart vehicle. That said, the Escalade-V's comfort and convenience are better than its bold performance. It comes with a 55-inch pillar-to-pillar screen for the gauge cluster, infotainment system, and passenger entertainment, plus two standard 12.6-inch screens for the second-row passengers. Leather and carbon fiber adorn the interior. A 36-speaker AKG surround-sound audio system is standard, along with so much more. The AMG GLS 63 is just as luxurious, with its heated, ventilated, and massaging front seats, among plenty of other features too long to list. Plus, we'd need a whole separate article to write about the Rolls-Royce Cullinan's features. Nevertheless, the Escalade-V's pure American excess is exactly why you should be considering it. A GLS might blend into the crowd, while the Cullinan costs more than twice as much as the Escalade-V. Choosing the Cadillac means having more eyes on you, as your SUV sounds like a Corvette rumbling, popping, and banging when you let off the accelerator. Sources: Cadillac, Mercedes-Benz, Rolls-Royce, CarEdge, iSeeCars, Classic.com We want to hear from you. Share your perspective in the comments below, and please keep the conversation respectful. They say the Escalade V-Series can go toe-to-toe with the likes of the Mercedes GLS 63 AMG or BMW XB7 Alpina! It looks great, has a fantastic powertrain, and the Escalade has a timeless cool factor. You can forget about Porsche—they’re going all-electric (BEV) now. With the RSQ7 and RSQ8, Audi caters to customers who want a taste of the German dream while in the US—so, not exactly the typical American buyer. Personally, I’m not a fan of SUVs, but if someone wants one, they should go for it—provided they buy or lease it with their own after-tax money. I dislike it when governments around the world subsidize these massive SUVs—whether they’re internal combustion (ICE) or BEVs, which are even bulkier and heavier, making them even more dangerous for smaller cars and pedestrians. title: Honda Reportedly Fast-Tracks Next-Gen CR-V, More Hybrids After Killing EVs - Road & Track
content: A new report suggests the next CR-V will begin production in early 2027. Honda took the axe to its whole EV operation earlier this year, leaving it with a few holes in its lineup. Now, it could be fast-tracking the development and launch of next-generation hybrid vehicles, starting with the CR-V. As reported by Nikkei, Honda is moving up the launch and production of its next-gen CR-V to February 2027. The current model isn’t especially old, considering it went on sale in late 2022 as a 2023 model year vehicle. That said, it’s Honda’s most popular vehicle here in the U.S., so keeping it competitive with other hybrid compact SUVs like the Toyota RAV4 (now hybrid-only) is vital. Nikkei reports that the CR-V that launches next year will be a full redesign of the current model. It’s set to be fitted with Honda’s next-generation hybrid technology, which we suspect will be an evolution of the company’s two-motor hybrid system it’s used for years. The report doesn’t specify whether or not this CR-V will be hybrid-only or continue to offer a purely gas-powered variant, but we wouldn’t be surprised to see Honda follow in Toyota’s footsteps and go all-in on its excellent hybrid powertrain. In addition to this Honda news, the report says Acura will launch a new hybrid vehicle based on this next-gen CR-V. The RDX has long been Acura’s CR-V-like SUV offering in terms of size and use case. However, Acura said in January that the next RDX was “planned for market introduction in the next couple of years,” suggesting it will launch much later than this next-gen CR-V. We already knew Honda was developing a three-row hybrid SUV based on previous reports, but this latest report from Nikkei further confirms the presence of such a vehicle. The plan would be for that model to launch in 2029. Instead of the four-cylinder two-motor hybrid powertrain, a V-6-based two-motor hybrid system is reportedly being developed that would power this large hybrid vehicle. Road & Track reached out to Honda about this report and received the following statement in response. “This was not announced by Honda. While we cannot comment on specific future product plans, as outlined in our 2026 Business Update, Honda remains on track to introduce next-generation HEV models beginning in 2027, featuring an all-new hybrid system and platform.” We may earn commission from links on this page, but we only recommend products we back.

title: V GIRLS: Freya Skye Is Writing Her Way Into Who She Is Becoming - V Magazine
content: At 16, Freya Skye is only beginning to see where the road might take her, with music as her north star. At 16, Freya Skye is only beginning to see where the road might take her, with music as her north star. Freya Skye was five years old when a karaoke machine appeared under the Christmas tree, and she has been singing ever since. At 13, she represented the UK at the Junior Eurovision Song Contest. By now, at 16, she has amassed over 2.5 billion streams and sold out more than a hundred shows worldwide. She also released a debut EP in February called Stardust that charted in both the US and UK. “I don’t really believe in coincidences,” she says of that first karaoke machine. “Music has always had a way of finding me or maybe I’ve always had a way of finding it.” Skye created Stardust with some of pop’s most in-demand names — like songwriter Julia Michaels and Grammy-winning producers Mattman and Robin, known for their work with Selena Gomez and Taylor Swift — but the songs are unmistakably hers. “Each song is a piece of who I was when I wrote it,” she says. “They’re messy, honest, and a little bit broken on their own but together they tell the full story.” Lead single “silent treatment,” about being ghosted without explanation, has clocked over 100M streams across all DSPs.”It’s not a hyper-specific story, it’s a specific feeling,” she says. “Everyone has been on one side of that silence or the other.” Writing with Michaels left a mark that went beyond the songs. “She’s so calm and grounded, genuinely kind to write with, and within ten minutes she knew everything about me because I’m an open book like that,” Skye says. “When someone that secure in themselves is sitting across from you, you end up writing braver.” Her shows have grown from 200-capacity rooms to 7,000-seat venues in under a year, and she has fought hard to keep them accessible — partnering with Ticketmaster to ensure her tour tickets can only be resold at face value. “Keeping tickets as affordable as possible is so important, especially with my fanbase where we’re all teenagers and young girls,” she says. “You never want to close people out.” The devotion goes both ways. “They’ve been queuing since seven that morning, dressed up, giving everything they have. I’m just giving it back to them.” Freya Skye’s latest single ‘Bad Taste’ arrived September 16 and is now available to stream across all platforms as she continues work on her debut album. Her film Zombies 5: Secrets of the Sea, in which she plays Nova, is now in production. Her world is only getting bigger, fashion included. In July, Hollister named her the face of its fall “Made for This Moment” denim campaign, a partnership that will also see the brand sponsor her upcoming tour dates across North America, the UK and Europe. She wears it all lightly: the Oscar de la Renta gown she wore at the Zombies 4: Dawn of the Vampires premiere made her feel “like a completely different, more grown-up version of myself for a night,” she says, though at home she’s happiest in “the comfiest thing I own, some huge hoodie.” Wherever it all goes next, Skye says, she’s ready for it, because her passion remains: “Music is the part of me I can never turn off.” This cover story appears in the pages of V162: now available for purchase! title: Coach V’s Corner: Running away from home - Post Independent
content: “There are years you think about for moments, and moments you think about for years.” I recently bumped into a pleasant young lady who I have known for years through our participation in the local softball league. On a normal day, I would have been thrilled at our meeting, given her a big hug and inquired as to the health and well-being of her family. But not on this sunny September morning. USC. Those letters stand for the University of Southern California, and they were stenciled in big, bold maroon letters across the front of her white T-shirt. She was surprised when, instead of the usual embrace, I took a step back, much like a vampire being exposed to the morning rays of the sun. “Oh goodness gracious,” were the only words I could think of to say. Her mom, who was standing close by, told me that her daughter had grown up in Southern California, so an allegiance to the Trojans of USC should not be such a shocking event for me. Being a good friend of the family, I felt compelled to explain to both of them why those three letters gave me such a start and also to recount the gloomy December day in 1974 when I ran away from home following USC’s 55-24 trouncing of my Notre Dame Fighting Irish. I was 14 years old and a devout fan of the Irish. I would get up early every Sunday morning in the fall so I could catch the immortal voices of Lindsey Nelson and Paul Hornung on the “Notre Dame Replay” show on Channel 2 out of Denver. We only got four television stations back then, and Channel 2 was my favorite because they showed all of the after-school favorites like “Blinky’s Fun Club,” “Gilligan’s Island” and “McHale’s Navy.” I got hooked on “All-Star Wrestling” on Sunday mornings, also on Channel 2. This game was on a Saturday afternoon, and there was no replay, although I have replayed the six touchdowns that Trojan running back Anthony Davis scored in the second half many times during the last five decades. Notre Dame actually made the first half look easy, racing to a 24-6 lead in Irish coach Ara Parseghian’s last regular-season game. The Irish had taken command in the old Los Angeles Coliseum, and I was strutting around the house bragging to any family member who would listen that Notre Dame could not be stopped on this day. One week following the game, the cover of Sports Illustrated featured Davis racing past Irish defenders en route to one of his six scores. The title on the cover shouted, “What a Comeback! USC and Anthony Davis Shatter Notre Dame.” And shatter them they did. Holding Notre Dame scoreless and tallying seven touchdowns of their own, the Trojans sent the Irish packing back to South Bend, Indiana, with their tails between their legs. As you can imagine, all members of the family that I was boasting to a few hours earlier took great pleasure in razzing me to tears as I raced upstairs and sequestered myself in my bedroom. Riddled with anger, I decided to sneak down the back outside stairway, run away from home and be done with all of these cruel people. My foray out into the real world lasted all of about two hours before darkness, the chill of December and the thought of Mom serving dinner without me drove me back to the friendly confines of home. I rolled into the kitchen of our home quietly, as if nothing had happened out of the ordinary, and took my place at the table. The meal was very good, as they always were under the direction of Bea Vidakovich. Not an unkind word was uttered about my cameo disappearance. I knew my dad would not let things go, though. He never did. Just before bedtime, I heard his heavy footfalls coming up the steps to my bedroom. He peeked his head in the doorway and simply told me that if I ever pulled a stunt like that again, he would give me something to run away about. That’s my running away from home story, and no, it’s never happened again. I appreciated being home, being young and having all of my family around. Why, even to this day, I sometimes imagine that I have on ruby slippers and I click the heels together, saying, “There’s no place like home.” I don’t have a dog named Toto, but I do have a cat named Houdini. I guess that’s all a guy could ask for. An avid runner, Mike Vidakovich is the girls basketball coach at Roaring Fork High School and a substitute teacher at Glenwood Springs Elementary.
